name: api/idempotency
summary: Make selected state-changing API operations safe to retry with an idempotency key.
intent: Clients can retry designated mutating requests after timeouts or network failures without accidentally executing the underlying operation more than once.

rules.text: Protected operations accept an explicit idempotency key from the client.
Repeating the same operation with the same key returns the stored result instead of executing the operation again.
Reusing a key for a materially different request is rejected as a conflict.
Keys are scoped narrowly enough that one caller or operation cannot accidentally replay another caller's result.

invariants.text: The application's existing error and response conventions remain intact.
Endpoints not opted into idempotency keep their existing behavior.
The idempotency record and protected side effect cannot diverge in a way that causes a successful operation to run twice.

acceptance.text: Two equivalent requests with the same key execute the protected side effect once and return an equivalent response.
The same key used with a different request fingerprint is rejected and does not execute the second side effect.
Concurrent requests racing on one key cannot both execute the protected operation.
Stored keys have an explicit retention policy and expired records can be cleaned up safely.
